title: Measure committees an elected official raised money for or lent a name to
question: Which ballot-measure committees are tied to an elected official by the filings themselves, who are their largest organization donors, and what business did those donors have before the same official?
finding: 127 gifts of $5,000 or more from organizations, firms and other committees, $8.6 million in all, went to committees tied to 17 officials: $3.4 million reported as given at an official's request, the rest to committees carrying an official's name. The Ethics Commission's November 2024 release on a mayoral candidate's two committees cites a $500 limit on contributions to a candidate's committee; measure committees have no limit, and the largest gift here is $550,000 from Emerson Collective LLC. Most went to committees tied to Daniel Lurie ($5.6 million) and London Breed ($1.1 million). 13 of the gifts ($1.3 million) came from donors the City paid $100,000 or more around the gift, or whose lobbyist contacted that official within a year, or whose contract that official or board approved within a year. Individuals gave a further $4.8 million at officials' request; they are counted (59) and not listed.
how: Two records tie a committee to an official. Form 114.5 is filed by a ballot-measure or independent committee when contributions of $5,000 or more were made at the request of a City elected officer, and names the officer and each contributor; repeated lines are counted once. Separately, measure and general-purpose committees are listed when the registered name presents the committee as belonging to a person who has filed a Form 700 as Mayor, Supervisor or another elected City officer (a possessive such as 'Mayor X's committee', 'supported by', 'an initiative of', or the person's name 'for' a measure), or when the filer record names that person as the committee's candidate; recall committees and committees for or against a candidate are left out. Their organization donors of $10,000 or more are shown, with a note where the person did not hold the office when the money came in (read from the terms of office the Board of Supervisors prints and from the years of the person's Form 700). Whether a contributor on Form 114.5 is a person is read from the committee's own contribution schedule. For each donor: City payments to a payee of the same name in the fiscal year of the gift and the years either side; lobbyists' reported contacts with that official for the donor as client within a year of a gift; and contract-approval notices (Form 126) naming the donor, filed for that officer or for the Board within a year.
limits: Asking donors to fund a ballot measure is disclosed on exactly these forms, and measures have no contribution limit; an official's name on a committee is a public endorsement. Large companies are paid by the City, lobby it and fund measures as a matter of course, so the three columns describe an overlap, not a favour, and none of them shows what, if anything, was decided for the donor. A committee named for a candidate who did not yet hold office is shown with that note. Donors are matched to payees and lobbying clients by name, so an affiliate under another name is missed. Committees an official controls without saying so in the name or on Form 114.5 cannot be seen. See the site’s “Each official’s circle” page for each official's wider circle and City dataset “Lobbyist Directory” (DataSF b947-pj2q) for lobbying money. The payment file labels each line with a fiscal year that is not always the year the payment was issued: some earlier payments, mostly on purchase orders in multi-year capital funds, are filed under a later year, and the Controller's own published figures follow that label. Payments are dated here by voucher number, a single running sequence, which moves $5.52 billion of $119.3 billion (4.6%) to an earlier year than its label; $1.08 billion of that belongs to fiscal 2018 or earlier, before the file starts. Near the turn of a year the number dates a payment to within a few days. Lines the file labels fiscal 2017 and 2018 are held only as yearly totals, so they keep the label; payments issued before July 2018 that the file labels with a later year are counted in fiscal 2018.
